metadata.case_name: CHU YUEN LING v. KWOK CHUEN AND OTHERS

injuries.description: Multiple lacerations of the face leading to permanent, conspicuous and unsightly scars, mainly on the left side of the face.
source: her head shattered the windscreen of the vehicle driven by her husband, in which she was a passenger, causing multiple lacerations of the face.
There are still multiple, conspicuous and unsightly scars, mainly on the left side of the face, with assymetry of the eyelids.

injuries.description: Deformity and disfigurement of the left upper and lower eyelid with a 2mm defect in the upper eyelashes and inability to close the left eye fully (gap of 8mm).
source:
Eyelids:
Left:
There is deformity and disfigurement of the upper and lower eyelid. The left eye appears to be much bigger than the right, due to a slight pull-down of the lower lid and a pull-up of the upper lid from scar contracture. There is a 2mm. defect in the upper eyelashes. The eyelids cannot close fully, when attempting to close there remains a gap of 8mm. through which the white of the eye appears, causing an unsightly appearance.
This girl has both a functional and a cosmetic disability from her accident. Her scars are permanent and will not alter significantly with time.

manifestations.description: multiple, conspicuous and unsightly scars, mainly on the left side of the face
The eyelids cannot close fully, when attempting to close there remains a gap of 8mm. through which the white of the eye appears, causing an unsightly appearance.

treatments_received: wounds were sutured at Kwong Wah Hospital
surgery to her left upper eyelid at Kwong Wah Hospital (three months after accident)
plastic surgery to her left facial scars at Princess Margaret Hospital (May, 1976)
treatments_future: further plastic surgery from a private practitioner in order to lessen her disability and improve her cosmetic appearance.
Plastic surgery could lessen her disability. Skin grafts would allow the eye to close normally and also make the opening symmetrical with the other eye.
Two admissions to a hospital would be necessary for the plastic surgery.

losses.description: Multiple conspicuous and unsightly scars, mainly on the left side of the face, with assymetry of the eyelids.

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: She feels reluctant to appear in public.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: No longer participates in such previous social activities as swimming, bowling and hiking.
